text:
Maya: FYI Northstar asked for a clear plan for the private POC credentials + HSM trust anchor. their security team is pushing for HSM-backed keys and offline key custody. can we confirm what handoff patterns we support?

Kai: we support two main flows: 1) customer-wrapped key import (you provide a key-encryption-key and we import) or 2) remote-signing via customer HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Thales using PKCS#11 agent). both have tradeoffs re: latency and controls.

Liam: ops note: remote-signing requires a short-lived mTLS tunnel from our private nodes to the customer's HSM endpoint. we'll need IP allowlist + port 17902 (our signer agent). also recommend a bastion/transit VPC endpoint for keywrap handshakes.

Rachel: compliance checklist items from our side: FIPS-validated HSM preferred, signed attestation of key policies, audit log forwarding to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS). if Northstar insists on offline custody we can support wrapped-key import with KMS key-wrapping (customer supplies encrypted key blob).

JJ (northstar): thanks. Our vendor is Thales nShield. they want either direct signing (preferred) or wrapped import with HSM-stamped metadata. offline custody means private key never leaves our HSM—so remote-signing is ideal. timeline: POC needs to start next week.

Maya: ok timeline noted. Kai / Liam, can we outline the minimal steps we need from Northstar to enable remote-signing? include certs, network, and test vector expectations. also give a billing impact note (dedicated pool + HSM connector).

Kai: minimal steps: 1) provide HSM endpoint (hostname + port) and PKCS#11 creds or TLS client cert for mutual auth. 2) provide CA chain for TLS and a signing cert subject to verify key usage. 3) test CSR/signing endpoint + sample signed payloads. Example PKCS#11 config snippet we ask for: 

```
pkcs11_module: /usr/lib/libnssckbi.so
slot: 1
pin_env: NORTHSTAR_HSM_PIN
label: redwood-signer-key
```

Kai: we'll run an integration in a preprod VPC. expected extra latency: ~5-20ms per sign depending on HSM.

Liam: networking checklist we'll send as a short doc, but essentials: 1) static egress IPs (we'll give) 2) allow inbound from our signer agent 17902 and 443 for control 3) MTU and keepalives for stable tunnels.

Rachel: security note: we require CRL/OCSP reachable for the supplied CA. rotation SOP: customer rotates keys in HSM -> we validate new certs via a canary route for 24h. fallback: auto-route to a pinned wrapped-key variant if remote-signing fails.

Maya: pricing impact: dedicated private + HSM connector is a small fixed monthly connector fee + nominal per-sign token surcharge. estimate for POC (2 weeks): waived connector fee, usage billed only. I'll confirm exact numbers in pricing deck.

deploy-bot: POC environment created: redwood-private-poc-northstar-02 (expires in 14 days). access: https://console.internal/redwood/poc/02.

JJ (northstar): perfect. next steps from our side: share PKCS#11 credentials in a signed ZIP via SFTP (we can't paste secrets in slack). who should I send to?

Maya: send to secure-uploads@redwood.ai and CC me + Kai. we'll pick up and schedule a 1hr integration window.

Kai: I'll draft the step-by-step integration checklist and a quick test harness (curl + sample payloads) and drop in the secure upload once we have creds. expected engineer time: ~4-6 hours to validate.

Liam: tagging infra on the integration: @oncall-infra. we'll provision the NAT/egress IPs and pre-stage the signer agent.

Rachel: I'll prepare the attestation template for Northstar legal to sign (HSM policy, key usage, audit retention).

Maya: thanks team — I'll update the customer and aim to lock the integration window for Thu 09:00 PT. JJ ping us if that conflicts. :thumbsup:

JJ (northstar): Thu 09:00 PT works. sending SFTP creds now via secure channel.

Kai: ack — will monitor the secure upload and confirm receipt.

Maya: recording action items: 
- Northstar: SFTP upload of PKCS#11 creds + CA chain (JJ)
- Maya: confirm pricing waiver for POC
- Kai: integration checklist + test harness
- Liam: provision egress IPs & signer agent
- Rachel: attestation template

Maya: any enterprise blockers still outstanding?

Rachel: one outstanding: Northstar's procurement asked for a SOC2+FIPS addendum. legal wants to see our evidence before extending dedicated for long-term. for POC we can proceed with a narrower data handling attestation.

JJ (northstar): we can accept a POC-scoped attestation. will loop procurement after the integration.

Maya: great — call scheduled. thanks all.
